% SCI-PTC v0.1 shared falsifiable predictions -- owner-review draft r0.3.
\section{Falsifiable edge predictions}
\label{sec:normative-predictions}

These are scientific oracles for later conformance and validation work. They
are not claims that an implementation has passed.

\PTCPrediction{001}{Disabled route identity}{Rationale }{D005}{SCI-MAP}{With PTC disabled, each PTC signal, fitted-state, coefficient, and PTC-route MAP product has product realization state \texttt{disabled}; any requested upstream terminal product remains distinct, and response availability remains a separate typed axis.}
\PTCPrediction{002}{Same-unit response loss}{Rationale 1.3}{D002,D014}{SCI-CAL}{A detector-common astronomical perturbation can retain mJy-per-fixed-nominal-beam units while being attenuated or annihilated; unit equality alone will not predict recovered amplitude.}
\PTCPrediction{003}{Correlation non-identification}{Rationale 1.2}{D004,D014}{None}{Two data sets with the same detector covariance but different physical mixtures admit the same fitted correlated subspace; the fit alone cannot distinguish atmosphere from sky or electronics.}
\PTCPrediction{004}{Gauge invariance}{Rationale 3.1}{D014,D015}{None}{Negating a basis/loading pair, reciprocally rescaling it, or rotating a degenerate basis leaves the fitted correlated signal and transformed output unchanged within declared numerical tolerance.}
\PTCPrediction{005}{Centering null mode}{Rationale 3.1}{D017}{None}{Changing detector-time data by a mode removed by the declared centering operator does not change the centered fit coordinate; that mode appears in the published additive-reference/null-space state.}
\PTCPrediction{006}{Scaling restoration}{Rationale 3.1}{D017}{None}{For an invertible internal scaling multiplied by a finite nonzero constant and consistently inverted, ordinary transformed output in the physical unit is unchanged within tolerance.}
\PTCPrediction{007}{Zero-fill is not exclusion}{Rationale 2.1}{D007,D010}{None}{Replacing one excluded nonzero sample by zero before ordinary PCA changes means/covariance and can change the selected subspace; a correctly masked/weighted missing-data estimator gives zero fit influence instead.}
\PTCPrediction{008}{Fit-excluded apply-allowed}{Rationale }{D007}{None}{An occurrence excluded from fitting but admitted for application is acted on by the exact frozen application map without affecting learned or selected state; toggling only its output support does not refit.}
\PTCPrediction{009}{Support-stage independence}{Rationale 2.1}{D007}{VAL}{Changing coefficient-only support changes the affected coefficient product but not the fitted basis or transformed signal; changing fit support invalidates or refits the fitted state.}
\PTCPrediction{010}{Influence through fitting}{Rationale 2.2}{D007}{VAL}{A single occurrence used to fit a common mode can influence subtractions at many other occurrences even where its direct local derivative is zero; those outputs carry transitive fit influence.}
\PTCPrediction{011}{Source-mask boundary}{Rationale 3.3}{D004,D014}{AST,ALIGN}{Moving a sample across a declared mask boundary changes fit/application behavior only according to the serialized polarity and boundary rule; unmasked sky remains eligible to project into the removed subspace.}
\PTCPrediction{012}{Within-array isolation}{Rationale 3.2}{D011}{None}{Changing data in another array does not change a base-v0.1 fitted subspace, rank, subtraction, or coefficient for the selected array.}
\PTCPrediction{013}{Hierarchy order materiality}{Rationale 3.2}{D011}{None}{For overlapping nonorthogonal array, network, and local components, sequential orders can produce different cumulative subspaces; the declared order reproduces the realized result and cannot be omitted from state.}
\PTCPrediction{014}{Common-mode denominator failure}{Rationale 4.1}{D010}{None}{A group/time with zero, empty, or non-finite admitted denominator yields unavailable/rejected state or a typed fallback, never a silently valid zero common mode.}
\PTCPrediction{015}{Fixed-template orthogonality}{Rationale 4.1}{D010}{None}{For a frozen fixed-template metric, a perturbation exactly orthogonal to the removed subspace is preserved by the conditional operator; learned-template motion is a separate full-procedure effect.}
\PTCPrediction{016}{Rank-deficient gauge}{Rationale 4.1}{D010,D012}{None}{Duplicate or zero columns produce a rank-deficient fit whose generalized inverse, tolerance, selected subspace, and deterministic tie rule reproduce the emitted subtraction.}
\PTCPrediction{017}{Least-aggressive selection}{Rationale 4.3}{D012}{Owner policy}{For nested candidates where the first two fail at least one required predicate and the third passes all, the third is selected even if an earlier candidate has a better scalar score.}
\PTCPrediction{018}{No compensating metric}{Rationale 4.3}{D012}{Owner policy}{A candidate with excellent residual suppression but failed astronomical-transfer predicate is rejected; residual improvement cannot compensate for sky-response failure.}
\PTCPrediction{019}{Deterministic tie}{Rationale 4.3}{D012}{Owner policy}{Two candidates equal under every required predicate and the declared ordering resolve identically across repeated execution using the registered tie rule.}
\PTCPrediction{020}{Empty candidate set}{Rationale 4.3}{D012}{Owner policy}{If no candidate passes all required predicates, no transformed product claiming admitted mode selection is produced.}
\PTCPrediction{021}{Immutable-parent refinement}{Rationale 5.2}{D009}{SCI-CAL}{A support-changing second refinement fit equals a fresh fit of the complete selected model on the immutable CAL parent and differs, in general, from fitting the already cleaned first output.}
\PTCPrediction{022}{Output-only classification}{Rationale 5.2}{D009}{VAL}{Changing one detector from retained to postfit-output-reject without changing fit support preserves the fitted subspace and other detectors' transformed values.}
\PTCPrediction{023}{Refinement oscillation}{Rationale 5.2}{D009}{Owner policy}{Alternating membership of a high-leverage detector reaches the declared oscillation/exhaustion state and is never labeled converged.}
\PTCPrediction{024}{Diagnostic population dependence}{Rationale 5.1}{D009}{Owner policy}{The same residual statistic can be ordinary under one declared population/noise reference and anomalous under another; the policy result changes only with an explicitly changed reference state.}
\PTCPrediction{025}{Diagnostic-only $r$ inertia}{Rationale 4.2}{D008,Q001}{SCI-RTC}{Changing an admitted conditioned-$r$ diagnostic while holding calibrated $x$ and all $x$ policy fixed can change only $r$ diagnostic outputs, not $x$ fit membership, subtraction, output, or coefficients.}
\PTCPrediction{026}{Raw-$r$ incompatibility}{Rationale 4.2}{D008}{SCI-RTC}{If conditioned-$r$ operator, unit, response, optical-leakage state, or exact $x$-grid relation is missing, the $r$ diagnostic branch is unavailable while the admitted $x$ branch may remain defined.}
\PTCPrediction{027}{Coefficient gauge}{Rationale 6.1}{D015}{None}{Reciprocal basis/loading rescaling changes fitted loading values but leaves the modeled subtraction unchanged; an analysis/gridding coefficient does not transform merely because a loading gauge changes.}
\PTCPrediction{028}{Coefficient normalization}{Rationale 6.1}{D015}{SCI-MAP}{Multiplying all raw gridding coefficients by a common nonzero factor can leave a normalized weighted estimate unchanged while changing the denominator, proving that the denominator is not automatically precision.}
\PTCPrediction{029}{Conditional covariance}{Rationale }{D014}{NOI}{For a fixed analytic $J_{\Theta}[Y]$ and declared $C_Y$, the conditional covariance equals $J_{\Theta}[Y]C_YJ_{\Theta}[Y]^{\mathsf T}$ including off-diagonal detector/time terms.}
\PTCPrediction{030}{Selection variance term}{Rationale 6.2}{D012,D014}{NOI}{Across perturbations that change rank or support, total output variance exceeds or differs from the mean conditional covariance whenever between-selection means vary.}
\PTCPrediction{031}{Fixed companion noninterference}{Rationale 7.1}{D013}{None}{Adding a response companion through the fixed-state path leaves fitted modes, rank, masks, detector classes, and transformed science data unchanged.}
\PTCPrediction{032}{Full-procedure nonlinearity}{Rationale 7.2}{D013}{None}{An injected source that crosses a rank, mask, clipping, classification, or convergence boundary produces amplitude- or side-dependent finite response rather than one global linear kernel.}
\PTCPrediction{033}{Package response boundary}{Rationale 7.2}{D013}{SCI-RTC,SCI-CAL}{Rerunning PTC from a fixed CAL parent can characterize PTC-full-procedure response but cannot expose a changed RTC or CAL learned state; that requires a separately named whole-chain study.}
\PTCPrediction{034}{Map-center factor availability}{Rationale 7.3}{D016}{SCI-MAP,BEAM}{Removing the exact source companion or named reference MAP operator makes the map-center diagnostic unavailable while leaving a supported sample-domain PTC response potentially available.}
\PTCPrediction{035}{Compact versus extended response}{Rationale 7.3}{D016}{BEAM}{A compact source and detector-common extended mode with equal nominal peak amplitude can have different PTC responses; the compact map-center diagnostic cannot predict the extended response.}
\PTCPrediction{036}{Random-state reproducibility}{Rationale 8.2}{D006}{None}{Repeating a simulation or randomized estimator with identical generator/version, seed, stream, and input identity reproduces the declared draws and realized result; changing one stream changes only its assigned draws.}
\PTCPrediction{037}{Required-output atomicity}{Rationale 8.1}{D005}{None}{Failure to publish one required sibling or link leaves the product explicitly incomplete; a remaining readable file cannot be labeled complete.}
\PTCPrediction{038}{Evidence-layer separation}{Rationale 9.2}{D006}{None}{Successful algebraic and document-coverage checks do not change implementation conformity, representation fidelity, observational performance, or production-readiness status from unassessed/not performed.}
\PTCPrediction{039}{Frozen component versus projection}{Rationale }{D010,Q002}{None}{For a perturbation with nonzero projection onto the frozen removed subspace, frozen-component subtraction has identity derivative while frozen-subspace application removes that projected component; the two responses differ even though both reproduce $Y-\widehat U$ on the fitted parent.}
\PTCPrediction{040}{Temporal versus detector action}{Rationale }{D010,Q002}{None}{For a nonsymmetric response matrix $H$, temporal-left projection $\mathcal L^t_{\Theta}H$ and detector-right projection $H\mathcal L^d_{\Theta}$ generally differ; matrix orientation and rank alone cannot select the propagated companion.}
\PTCPrediction{041}{No double upstream response}{Rationale 7.1}{D013}{SCI-CAL}{Propagating a CAL-grid companion through $J_{\Theta}[Y]$ gives the same result as propagating its source-domain parent through $J_{\Theta}[Y]\circ K_{\rm up\to CAL}$ exactly once; applying $K_{\rm up\to CAL}$ again changes the domain or value and is rejected.}
\PTCPrediction{042}{Typed procedure state change}{Rationale }{D013}{None}{A perturbation that changes selected rank yields a valid transformed-signal finite difference and a separate typed rank change; attempting to subtract the complete procedure tuples is undefined and cannot produce the response.}
\PTCPrediction{043}{Candidate-evidence reconstruction}{Rationale }{D012}{Owner policy}{Given the retained candidate order, fitted states, predicate values, causes, and tie rule, the selected or rejected disposition is reproduced exactly; removing one failed predicate record makes the selection audit incomplete.}
\PTCPrediction{044}{External-parent fail-closed}{Rationale }{D004,D014}{FRUIT}{Removing the recurrence identity or coordinate registration from an otherwise numerical source/residual parent makes the affected protected or fitted role unavailable while leaving independent PTC roles unchanged.}
\PTCPrediction{045}{Surrogate support transformation}{Rationale }{D006,D007}{VAL,NOI}{Shifting surrogate signal without shifting its associated validity/eligibility changes admitted support and fails the surrogate contract; shifting both together reproduces the declared transformed membership, while insufficient support is rejected rather than zero-filled.}
\PTCPrediction{046}{Astronomical-predicate typing}{Rationale }{D012,D013}{Owner policy}{Two candidates with the same scalar transfer value but different source class, response type, amplitude/location domain, or uncertainty treatment do not satisfy the same astronomical-transfer predicate and cannot be substituted.}
\PTCPrediction{047}{Unavailable bias claim}{Rationale }{D010,D014}{NOI}{When an estimator family supplies no expectation/bias statement for data-dependent selection, the bias claim remains unavailable even if one synthetic realization has zero measured residual mean.}
\PTCPrediction{048}{Independent product and response states}{Rationale }{D005,D013}{None}{An otherwise realized transformed signal can coexist with unavailable complete response, while a disabled PTC product has no realized signal even if an upstream CAL response exists; neither state can be inferred from the other.}

\PTCPrediction{049}{Undefined fit-excluded extension}{Rationale 4.2}{D007,D010}{None}{For a fit-excluded occurrence missing any basis coefficient or coefficient-recomputation input, neighboring support, detector binding, metric term, coordinate transform, or boundary state required by the resolved operator, application is unavailable. Filling, interpolating, or reconstructing that occurrence changes the declared operator and cannot reproduce the authorized fit-excluded/apply-allowed result.}
